facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: Having reached the mountain Kailāsa, the lord Śiva of great sports entered his mansion along with his Gaṇas.
facts.text: The Shiva Purana describes Mount Kailash as the eternal sacred abode where Lord Shiva resides in meditation alongside Goddess Parvati.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: As the dew is dried up by the morning sun, so are the sins of mankind cleansed at the sight of Himachal.
facts.text: The Skanda Purana proclaims that the sins of mankind are cleansed at the sight of the Himalayas and the sacred peak of Kailash just as morning dew evaporates in the sun.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: He who undertakes the pilgrimage and circumambulation of Manasarovara and Kailasa attains the highest spiritual fruit and reaches the abode of Shiva.
facts.text: The Skanda Purana in the Manasa Khanda states that circumambulating Lake Manasarovar and Mount Kailash confers supreme spiritual merit upon the pilgrim.

facts.label: legend
facts.quote: Milarepa caught the first ray of the morning sun and arrived on the top of Mount Kailash without effort.
facts.source_name: The Life of Milarepa (Lobsang P. Lhalungpa translation)
facts.text: Tibetan religious lore maintains that the eleventh-century tantric yogi Milarepa was the only human ever to reach the summit of Mount Kailash by riding the rays of the morning sun.

facts.label: legend
facts.quote: Pilgrims often share urban legends claiming rapid biological aging and extraordinary nail growth while in proximity to the sacred mountain.
facts.text: Popular modern folklore alleges that travellers in close proximity to Mount Kailash undergo rapid biological aging, claiming fingernails and hair grow several weeks' worth in just 12 hours.

facts.label: disputed
facts.quote: Reinhold Messner pointed out that Mount Kailash could be climbed technically, but should not be summited due to sacred traditions, which led authorities to enforce strict permit bans.
facts.text: While esoteric legends assert Mount Kailash cannot be climbed because of supernatural barriers, mountaineers and alpine historians explain that the 6,638-metre peak is physically climbable and remains unclimbed solely because official permits are completely prohibited out of deference to religious sanctity.

facts.label: disputed
facts.quote: Traditional beliefs place the origin of four great Asian rivers directly at the foot of Mount Kailash, whereas remote hydrological mapping shows the headwaters originate in separate glaciers across the broader Gangdise range.
facts.source_name: Chinese Academy of Sciences Hydrological Studies
facts.text: While cultural tradition holds that 4 major Asian rivers emerge directly from the four faces of Mount Kailash, hydrologists demonstrate that the glacial source streams of the Indus, Sutlej, Brahmaputra, and Karnali originate from distinct valleys miles away across the Gangdise range.

facts.label: disputed
facts.quote: Mount Kailash consists of Paleogene conglomerate and sandstone strata sculpted naturally by glacial processes rather than artificial human architecture.
facts.source_name: Geological Society of America Special Papers
facts.text: While fringe writers claim that Mount Kailash is an artificial pyramid built by an ancient civilization, field geologists determine that its stratified shape is entirely natural, formed by tectonic uplift and quaternary glacial erosion.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: Archaeological excavations at the Piyang-Donggar site in Zanda County revealed over a thousand cave habitations and ancient burial chambers.
facts.source_name: Center for Tibetan Studies of Sichuan University
facts.text: Between 1997 and 2001, the Department of Archaeology of Sichuan University and the Bureau of Cultural Relics of the Tibet Autonomous Region excavated the Piyang-Donggar site in Ngari, recording over 1,000 cave chambers, Buddhist murals, and ancient burials.
